*Wörterbuch Romani\-Deutsch\-Englisch für den südosteuropäischen Raum: Mit einer Grammatik der Dialektvarianten*\.
Harrassowitz, Wiesbaden, 1994\.

The appendix deliberately covers “alte Etyma aus allen Dialekten” of European Romani rather than only the southeastern varieties of the dictionary proper, and cites every word in the shape it carries as a main entry there\. The scanned copy lacks the volume's front matter, so its abbreviation key and transcription description were not available; the source abbreviations used in the lists were resolved from the printed Literaturverzeichnis\.
references.progress: The etymological appendix “Etymologien” on printed pages 311--338 only, i.e. its four alphabetical word lists: Indische Etyma (pp. 311--328), Iranische Etyma (pp. 329--331), Armenische Etyma (pp. 331--332) and Griechische Etyma (pp. 333--338). Every printed entry in those lists is represented. Excludes the A--Z Romani-German-English dictionary (pp. 1--310), the German-Romani and English-Romani reverse indexes (pp. 339--362), the Variantengrammatik (pp. 363--417) and the Literaturverzeichnis (pp. 417--418). The “s. X” cross-reference lines inside the lists are pointers to a full entry elsewhere in the same appendix and are recorded in the audit rather than installed as forms

references.source:
Norbert Boretzky and Birgit Igla\.
*Wörterbuch Romani\-Deutsch\-Englisch für den südosteuropäischen Raum: Mit einer Grammatik der Dialektvarianten*\.
Harrassowitz, Wiesbaden, 1994\.
ISBN 9783447034593\.
The appendix deliberately covers “alte Etyma aus allen Dialekten” of European Romani rather than only the southeastern varieties of the dictionary proper, and cites every word in the shape it carries as a main entry there\. The scanned copy lacks the volume's front matter, so its abbreviation key and transcription description were not available; the source abbreviations used in the lists were resolved from the printed Literaturverzeichnis\.
references.progress: The etymological appendix “Etymologien” on printed pages 311--338 only, i.e. its four alphabetical word lists: Indische Etyma (pp. 311--328), Iranische Etyma (pp. 329--331), Armenische Etyma (pp. 331--332) and Griechische Etyma (pp. 333--338). Every printed entry in those lists is represented. Excludes the A--Z Romani-German-English dictionary (pp. 1--310), the German-Romani and English-Romani reverse indexes (pp. 339--362), the Variantengrammatik (pp. 363--417) and the Literaturverzeichnis (pp. 417--418). The “s. X” cross-reference lines inside the lists are pointers to a full entry elsewhere in the same appendix and are recorded in the audit rather than installed as forms

origin_lemma.etymology: 48 akṣōṭa m. 'walnut (or pistacio nut ?)' Kālid., 'Aleurites triloba, Croton moluccanum' Suśr., 'a mountain-tree pīlú-¹', lex.; akṣōḍa-, °aka-, ākṣōḍa-, ākhōṭa- lex. — lw. in Ir. Ormuri waṭk < *akhōṭa- Morgenstierne IIFL i 412.14197 akṣōṭa [Poss. ext. of akṣa- (akṣa-² 'seed of Elaeocarpus ganitrus') with suffix -ṭa- (as in śarkōṭá- 'scorpion' AV. Wackernagel-Debrunner Suffixes 514) beside Ir. *axša-ra- in Oss. äxsärä H. W. Bailey BSOAS 20, 58. NIA. forms with -r- may then be < *akṣarōṭṭa- (cf. dimin. suffix -uṭṭa- in WPah. (e.g. Varma BhalDial 23). M. akroḍ (~ akroṭ) is X akhoḍ rather than < *akṣarōṭṭa-]
